title: Loop status
description: What is true right now for every loop and concern of one project, as loop-status derives it from facts: the board, the queue of what needs a person, and what agents can start now. The loop-status script writes it with --json, and every reader of a project's status reads exactly this. schema_version is the version of this file; raise it whenever a change would make a reader of the previous version misread a document, and update every fixture and reader in the same change.

schema_version.description: The version of this schema that the document was written for.

project.description: The key of the project the document describes, usually its repository as owner/name. Every document describes exactly one project.

as_of.description: When the facts were gathered, in UTC. It is one of the facts, so deriving twice from the same facts gives the same document.

environments.description: Every environment in LOOP.md §3, lowest first, with the commit it serves or why that could not be read.

queue.description: What needs a person (the board's 'Needs you'), most unblocking first: sorted by the length of unblocks, longest first.

agents_can_start.description: Work an agent can start now without a person: ready concerns to build, shipped and stale ones to prove, incomplete contracts to design.

drift.description: Documents whose text the facts contradict, and other drift the board flags.

missing.description: Facts that could not be read for the whole project, such as pull requests when the forge is unreachable. Whatever depends on them is unknown.

id.description: A loop's folder name or a concern's file name without .md.

sha.description: A commit, abbreviated to at least 7 hex digits or in full.

concern_state.description: A concern's state: exactly the rows of the derivation table in loop-status SKILL.md, in its order, plus unknown when a fact the state depends on cannot be read. Finer detail ('in review', 'proving') belongs in the reason, never in the state.

loop_state.description: A loop's state, as step 5 of loop-status SKILL.md derives it, plus unknown when a fact it depends on cannot be read.

ci_state.description: The combined result of the checks on a commit: none when no check ran, unknown when it could not be read.

queue_kind.description: What a queue item asks of a person: one kind for each item loop-status queues in step 6 and offers in its Record step. A person acts on the first four: answer a question, review a pull request, ship to an environment, or approve a record. The rest are shown read-only, with the command to run: a proof that waits on a person, a fact only a person can read (command-center/D76), a concern that leads to no one (command-center/D77), a contradiction that needs a call, and a loop-document pull request that check_loop_pr.sh refused.

main.description: The main branch: its head and the result of its checks.

environment.description: An environment and the commit it serves. Exactly one of served and error is set: an environment that cannot be read is unknown, never assumed.

path.description: The loop's README, relative to the repository root.

reason.description: The facts behind the state, in one line.

next.description: The command or action that moves the loop on, or null.

owner.description: The loop's owner: from its front matter, else LOOP.md's owner; null until known.

members.description: The loop's members, from its front matter.

path.description: The concern's file, relative to the repository root.

claims.description: The concern's claims (C#), in the order of Done when.

reason.description: The facts behind the state, in one line, such as which table row matched and why.

next.description: The table's Next for this state, as a command where it is one; null when there is nothing to do.

contract.description: The concern's front matter. An entry that is absent is an empty list or null.

parked.description: The D# that parks the concern.

claim.description: A claim (C#) or a goal (G#), with every evidence line about it.

struck.description: True when the claim is struck through (superseded); it then counts for no state.

evidence.description: Its evidence lines, in file order; the last is the latest verdict.

current_holds.description: Whether it has a current HOLDS on the concern's ships-to environment (for a goal, on the loop's); null when that cannot be read.

evidence.description: One evidence line: YYYY-MM-DD · C1 · HOLDS · rung 1 · staging @<sha> · <evidence>.

commit.description: The commit it cites; null for @? (migrated without a commit), which never counts as a HOLDS.

inputs.description: The facts the state came from. The fields named here have fixed meanings; the derivation may add other facts.

main.description: The main branch's head that was read.

prs.description: The linked pull requests: by head branch, by Concern trailer in the body, or listed in prs.

commits.description: Commits on main that carry the concern's Concern trailer.

missing.description: The facts that could not be read, each with why; set whenever the state is unknown.

served.description: The commit the concern's ships-to environment serves, or why it could not be read (exactly one of the two), and whether it serves every merge commit of the concern.

environment.description: The ships-to environment; null when the contract has none.

serves.description: Whether the served commit has every merge commit of the concern as an ancestor; false when nothing is merged; null when unknown.

on_main.description: Whether merge_commit is on its repository's main. Only then does the pull request count as merged. Null when it has no merge commit or that could not be read.

queue_item.description: Something that needs a person. detail's shape follows kind.

id.description: A key that stays the same across runs while the item stands, such as <loop>/<concern>/Q1 or <owner>/<repo>#12.

title.description: One line to show for it.

why.description: Why it is in the queue, from the facts.

loop.description: The loop it belongs to; null when it spans loops, as a ship can.

unblocks.description: The concerns that finishing it unblocks, counting through needs across loops. Its length orders the queue.

waits_on.description: The one person it waits on: the holder of its gate in LOOP.md §2 when it crosses one, otherwise the loop's owner. Null until addressing fills it.

visible_to.description: The loop's members, who can see it but not act on it. Empty until addressing fills it.

gate.description: The gate in LOOP.md §2 it crosses, or null.

question_detail.description: An open question (Q#). Its options, its recommendation and its default are kept apart: the recommendation is the answer the file recommends, and the default is what happens if nobody answers. A question written before options were recorded has no options and no recommendation, and shows only the question, what it blocks and its default.

options.description: The options the file records, in its order, each with its main consequence; none is pre-selected. Empty for a question written before options were recorded.

recommendation.description: The text of the option the file recommends, exactly as that option has it, or null when it recommends none; always null when there are no options, and never the default. JSON Schema cannot tie it to an option, so whatever writes a document must, and this schema's tests check it for every fixture.

default.description: What happens if nobody answers: the Questions table's 'Default if unanswered', as written; null when that cell is empty.

blocks.description: What it blocks, as written in the Questions table.

option.description: One answer to a question, with its main consequence.

text.description: The option, as the file writes it.

consequence.description: What choosing it means, as the file writes it.

review_detail.description: A pull request ready for review.

proof.description: The body's 'How it was proven before the merge' section, as Markdown; null if the body has none.

ship_detail.description: Merged concerns waiting to ship to an environment.

manual_steps.description: The concerns' declared effects, as the steps a person performs.

record_detail.description: Text to write on the person's yes, and where.

proof_detail.description: An UNPROVEN claim that waits on a person: the one its line's `· needs <who>: <what>` names, or the loop's owner when the line names no one (command-center/D74, D75). Shown read-only, with the command to run once that is to hand.

environment.description: The environment the claim must be proven on.

missing.description: What the proof needs that no agent has, from its UNPROVEN evidence line.

supplied_by.description: Who can supply it: what the line's needs segment names (a login, owner, or gate:<key>), a person or role an older line's prose names, or owner when it names no one.

command.description: The command to run once it is to hand, such as /loop-prove <loop>/<concern> <env>.

fact_detail.description: A fact only a person can read: a LOOP.md §3 row that agents may not read, or that has no served-commit command, while an unfinished concern's state rests on it (command-center/D76). Shown read-only, with the command to run once it can be read.

fact.description: The fact, such as <environment>'s served commit.

environment.description: The LOOP.md §3 row it belongs to.

error.description: Why an agent cannot read it, as the board's missing facts say.

supplied_by.description: Who can read it: owner, the loop's owner.

next.description: What makes it readable, as the first concern resting on it says.

command.description: The command to run once it can be read: /loop-status <loop>.

stuck_detail.description: A concern that is neither done nor parked and leads to no one: no other queue item, no step an agent can take alone, and no need that leads anywhere (command-center/D77). Shown read-only, so its loop's owner can say what moves it.

reason.description: The concern's reason, from the facts.

next.description: The concern's next step, as the board gives it.

command.description: The command to run once something leads from it: /loop-status <loop>/<concern>.

contradiction_detail.description: A claim whose latest verdict is CONTRADICTS, with no decision dated after it, so it needs a call: redesign, or roll back. Shown read-only, with the command to run.

contradicts.description: What the evidence contradicts: the design text it disproves, or the shared decision (<loop>/D#) it says it contradicts.

escalates.description: True when the evidence line says it contradicts a shared decision, which escalates to the loop as a question.

command.description: The command to run, such as /loop-design <loop>/<concern>, or /loop-diagnose when the cause is unknown.

refused_pr_detail.description: A loop-document pull request that loop-status's check_loop_pr.sh refused, so no agent may merge it under LOOP.md §2.1. Shown read-only, with the command to run.

failures.description: The lines the checker printed for why it refused, in its order.

command.description: The command to run, such as the checker again: scripts/check_loop_pr.sh --pr <n>.
The command to run, such as /loop-build <loop>/<concern>.

where.description: The file and the place in it, or the concerns involved.

finding.description: What the text says, and what is actually true.
